summary: Read-only review complete. One omitted lock cycle and one invalidation-inventory discrepancy remain. No edits, builds, tests, network access, or .env reads performed.

findings.title: Magic-link consumption still reverses the customer-to-token lock order
findings.detail: auth/magic-link.ts:71-80 claims customer_token before routes/auth.ts:643-645 updates the customer or acquires its session-insert FK lock. Email-change consumption and erasure hold customer FOR UPDATE before updating/deleting that same token. A consumer holding the token and an email change holding the customer therefore deadlock. The resolver restructuring does not touch this path. Moving the customer lock earlier also requires accounting for grantSignupBonus's loyalty advisory lock. Replace the duplicate concurrency paragraph at line 195 with the following text.
findings.fix: Existing mailbox-token consumption is also restructured. `POST /v1/shop/auth/magic-link/consume` and `POST /v1/shop/auth/verify-email` first identify the token's customer without locking or consuming the token. In their mutation transaction, acquire the existing `lockCustomerLoyalty` advisory lock before the customer row, then acquire that customer `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`, constrained by customer and store, and reject a missing owner. This owner lock conflicts with recovery, email change, erasure and passkey operations while remaining compatible with commerce's customer foreign-key `KEY SHARE` locks. Only then atomically claim the exact token with hash, customer, store, kind, unused and `expires_at > clock_timestamp()` predicates. Preserve token consumption, email verification, signup bonus and, for magic links, session creation in the same transaction; failed claims perform none of those effects. `consumeMagicLink` must require this caller-held lock discipline. Both routes acquire the loyalty lock before the customer lock so neither retains the reverse customer-to-loyalty order through `grantSignupBonus`. Add deterministic real-route races against email-change consumption and erasure, with verified and unverified customers and signup bonuses enabled and disabled, plus concurrent loyalty checkout. Cover both lock interleavings without retries or sleeps: invalidation winning prevents token consumption and session issuance; consumption winning completes before invalidation proceeds; no deadlock occurs.

findings.title: Password reset does not currently burn all mailbox tokens
findings.detail: routes/customer-tokens.ts:140-141 marks only password_reset and email_change tokens used. It does not burn passkey_manage tokens, contrary to this matrix row and the §5 reset row. Epoch comparison and session revocation still prevent their use, but the claimed explicit invalidation and previous-image evidence are inaccurate. Replace this matrix row with the following text, which explicitly specifies the missing new-image deletion.
findings.fix: | Customer password reset (mailbox) | n/a | n/a | n/a | epoch + del | epoch + del; the new image explicitly deletes this customer's `passkey_manage` tokens in the same owner-locked reset transaction, alongside C/P/G deletion. The existing reset only burns `password_reset` and `email_change` tokens. During previous-image rollback, M remains stored but is unusable because its epoch differs and its bound session is revoked; test that distinction. | sessions revoked |
